newsitem.title: USA: Fed candidates' background checks nearly complete.
newsitem.headline: Fed candidates' background checks nearly complete.

text.p: U.S. officials are nearing the end of background checks in preparation for formal announcement of two candidates to fill Federal Reserve Board gubernatorial vacancies, said White House spokesman Mike McCurry on Friday.
"The background checking is proceeding satisfactorily and they're getting closer to the end stages of the process," McCurry said.

The White House in April confirmed that Roger Ferguson of consulting firm McKinsey and Co Inc and Edward Gramlich, a University of Michigan economics professor, have been chosen to fill the two Fed positions.

The two Fed vacancies opened earlier this year with the departure of Janet Yellen for the White House Council of Economic Advisers and Lawrence Lindsey for the conservative American Enterprise think tank.

Once background checks are completed and the candidates are formally nominated, they would face a confirmation hearing before the Senate Banking Committee and a full-Senate vote before becoming governors.
